ca_mcleod_lake_climbs.blurb: A small cliff just east of McLeod Lake in the high country above Mammoth Lakes, sitting around 9,300 feet. The dozen routes are short single pitches of roughly 50 to 70 feet, with a handful of easy lines in the 5.4 to 5.8 range and a solid core of 5.10s plus one 5.11. Climbs mix bolted and gear-protected lines. The stone is good but a little dirty in places, so test holds. Because it looks east it stays cool through summer afternoons, while snow can hang around the base into late June. It sees far fewer people than the nearby Horseshoe Slabs, which makes it a handy alternative when those are busy.
ca_mcleod_lake_climbs.parking_note: Leave the car in the Horseshoe Lake lot at the end of Lake Mary Road above the town of Mammoth Lakes.
ca_mcleod_lake_climbs.approach: From the Horseshoe Lake lot, take the trail toward McLeod Lake, then branch left onto a faint path. Cross a streambed that is usually dry by August and work left below broken rocks to the cliff, whose prominent arete and overhang are easy to spot.

ca_houda_north.blurb: A seaside bouldering sector on the north, west and south faces of Houda Point, near Trinidad in Humboldt County. It holds a dozen problems, most of them between V0 and V3, including a well-liked easy traverse for beginners and a jugs boulder with steep, fun lines. A few much harder problems reach the V9 to V11 range. A trail with stairs drops from the clifftop to the beach, and which side you take depends on the tide. Landings are sand when the beach is built up, but in winter they can turn into a jumble of 2 to 3 foot cobbles. Summer and fall are the best seasons here.

ca_voyager_rock.blurb: A granite dome on the east side of Courtright Reservoir in the southern Sierra, at roughly 8,500 feet in the Sierra National Forest. The twelve climbs are mostly crack-oriented trad lines, with a few bolted or top-rope options and an aid line or two. Difficulty is on the stiff side for a mountain crag: one easy route near 5.7, a 5.9, and then mainly 5.10 through 5.12, with five at 5.11. A rappel line down the dome was added in 2021. Visitors are few, so you will likely have the rock mostly to yourself on a cool, sunny day.

ca_atlantis_wall_right.blurb: The section of Atlantis Wall to the right of the Minotaur Wall, in the Lost Horse area of Joshua Tree National Park. All twelve routes are traditional, running from easy fifth class through the 5.5 to 5.8 range, with a couple of tougher lines at 5.10 and 5.11. The climbs are short and fairly steep, and the walk-off is easy, so the wall is a favourite for guided classes and top-rope groups. It sits in a canyon sheltered from the west, which can make it sweltering on a hot day, so cooler weather is much more pleasant.
